# Core tag-release controls and recovery

This is a disabled proposal. Both the prerequisite verification job and publication job have independent false guards; any separately authorized activation must review both. Do not enable or dispatch publication without separate authorization, a verified immutable protected tag ruleset, protected `main` first-parent merge policy, and a properly protected `core-production-release` environment. `github.ref_protected` only says some protection applies; it does not prove that tag updates/deletions or privileged bypass are prohibited. Check those controls independently. Use the protected immutable production tag as the release authorization; do not require routine environment reviewers. Restrict permitted tags and protect environment configuration against changes and bypass where supported. Configure `CORE_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT_READY=yes` at environment scope only, verify no repository or organization fallback exists, and protect that configuration. The sentinel is not proof that reviews remain enforced.

Configure a new direct-publish npm trusted publisher only after separate approval, while retaining the stage-only publisher. The proposed exact identity is repository `martletdesign/core`, workflow `tag-release.yml`, environment `core-production-release`. Ensure npm uses OIDC without a static token and verify provenance in an authorized integration rehearsal. A registry 404 cannot detect private staged-version reservations or prevent publication races; npm is the final authority. Confirm no new tag collides with historical `/theme` tags.

The proposed workflow rejects any already-published version before publishing and checks the registry again immediately before publication. It publishes only the inspected isolated tarball and creates a GitHub Release only after the registry metadata and downloaded bytes match. A successful npm publish is irreversible. If publication succeeds but verification or GitHub Release creation fails, do not rerun the publication job: it will reject the now-existing version. An authorized maintainer must independently inspect the npm package and provenance, confirm the unchanged protected tag and first-parent production commit, reproduce the same tarball, and run `RELEASE_TAG=vX.Y.Z node scripts/tag-release-cli.mjs verify-registry /absolute/path/to/reproduced.tgz`. Record the local SHA-512, registry integrity, package identity, provenance and tag SHA. After confirming the original authorized tag, package bytes and provenance, the maintainer may recover or reconcile the GitHub Release for that same tag; if a security mismatch is found, stop for review. If bytes or provenance differ, stop and investigate; never republish the version or move its tag.

For provenance recovery, install the exact published version in an empty disposable consumer with `npm install --ignore-scripts --legacy-peer-deps --save-exact <package>@<exact-version>`, then run `npm audit signatures --json --include-attestations > audit.json`. The audit must exit successfully and validate the Sigstore bundle. With `RELEASE_TAG` set to the original tag and `GITHUB_SHA` to its independently verified commit, run `node scripts/tag-release-cli.mjs verify-provenance audit.json /absolute/path/to/reproduced.tgz`. The checker requires a verified SLSA statement for the exact package bytes, tag, repository, release workflow and source commit. If the audit cannot reach its verification services or any assertion fails, treat provenance as unverified and do not create a release. The audit result is trusted only when freshly produced by the successful npm command.

The recovery procedure is manual and has not exercised a real npm publication or GitHub Release in this proposal. Existing `core-stage.yml` and its stage-only publisher remain unchanged; the release-event direct-publish job remains disabled. Any later decision to retire or reconcile the staged path requires separate review.
